description: One thing on this host that can cause code to run without a person: a systemd unit or timer, a cron entry, a shell init file, a PAM or sudoers rule, ld.so.preload, or a loaded kernel module. Current state; the history is in Persistence Change.

fields.label: Identifier
fields.description: Unique within its kind — a unit name, or the path of a cron file. Small Text because a real path exceeds what Data holds.

fields.label: Content Hash
fields.description: SHA-256 of the file. The content itself is never stored — a sudoers or PAM file is not something this app should hold a copy of.

fields.label: Owning Package
fields.description: The dpkg package that ships this file, if any. Nearly everything on a normal host belongs to one; the exceptions are the local additions and anything an attacker installed.

fields.label: Accepted As Baseline
fields.description: Set only by an explicit accept. A host rebuilt from a snapshot of a compromised one would otherwise normalise its own malware on first scan, which is exactly the situation these servers are in.

fields.label: Directives
fields.description: ExecStart, User, Restart, Description for a unit; the command lines for a crontab. Enough to judge it without reading the file again.

name: Persistence Item
